confirmed.evidence: For ACHE (P22303) this returns canonical 32-614 = the full mature chain, 583 aa, used for 4 of the 10 candidates in study #9 (data/study_candidate_screen.json: "basis": "mature_chain", "canonical_span": [32, 614]). That chain ends with the 40-residue AChE-T 't-peptide' / WAT domain, canonical 575-614 = mature 544-583, sequence DTLDEAERQWKAEFHRWSSYMVHWKNQFDHYSKQDRCSDL, containing three Trp and the free interchain Cys580 (mature). Counting cysteines in the construct gives 7 - odd parity - because Cys580's partner is a second AChE subunit or ColQ/PRiMA, which is absent. I parsed the stored models at /tmp/cbc_screen/*/boltz_results_input/predictions/input/input_model_0.cif and computed receptor residues within 5 A of the peptide chain: HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 native has 19 of 32 interface residues inside mature 544-583; BasalAChE-Abeta-B4 native has 18 of 31. Neither contacts the CAS or the PAS. Mean pLDDT over mature 544-583 is 66.5 and 62.0 against 95.5 and 95.1 for the catalytic domain 1-543. Decoys land there too (decoy1: 17 of 46). README.md:452-457 states the opposite is safe: "AChE carries no transmembrane feature, so its construct is byte-identical under both protocols and those cells were reused rather than recomputed."
confirmed.why_wrong: The topological argument in the docstring - 'soluble, so every residue is on the ligand's side' - is not sufficient. The t-peptide is not a solvent-exposed feature of the AChE monomer in vivo: it is an amphipathic helix that assembles into a four-helix bundle with the PRAD of ColQ/PRiMA or with sister subunits, and it carries an obligate interchain disulfide. Folded as a lone chain it presents ~40 residues of exposed Trp-rich amphipathic surface plus an unpaired thiol. That is the identical artefact the v1->v2 supersession was raised to eliminate for membrane receptors ('solvent-exposed hydrophobic surface that a structure predictor will dock a hydrophobic peptide onto'), and here the repo's own models show it dominating the scored interface for half the AChE arm. The AChE ipTMs in studies #9, #10 and #11 are therefore measuring a contact that cannot form on an assembled AChE oligomer. The repo also applies the odd-cysteine test to peptides (validate.py cysteine_parity) but not to the receptor construct it builds.
confirmed.fix: Treat obligate-oligomerisation segments the same way as transmembrane segments. For ACHE, end the construct at the catalytic domain (mature 1-543 / canonical 32-574, the span every human AChE crystal construct uses) and record the truncation in construct_basis as e.g. 'catalytic_domain' with the excluded span and its reason. Add a registry-level check that the construct has even cysteine parity, or that any odd cysteine is annotated as intra-construct. Re-run or explicitly retract the AChE cells of #9/#10/#11 rather than reusing them, and correct README.md:452-457, which currently asserts AChE needed no construct correction.

confirmed.claim: "PfcACh-PAM-P1": "CHRNA7",   # folded as st.Chain("A", rseq, "protein") - one copy of canonical 23-233
confirmed.evidence: The construct is a single copy of the CHRNA7 extracellular domain (data/study_candidate_screen.json: "canonical_span": [23, 233], 211 aa). The record's declared site is "α7 nAChR Extracellular Domain (ECD) (Tyr188, Trp149, Tyr195)", which this repo's own registry resolves in mature numbering (offset +22), i.e. canonical 210, 171, 217 - all inside the folded construct. Contact analysis of the four stored models (native + 3 decoys, /tmp/cbc_screen/PfcACh-PAM-P1_*/.../input_model_0.cif, receptor residues within 5 A of the peptide, construct index = mature index) gives: native contacts 93, 149, 150, 151, 190, 191, 192, 193, 195; decoy0 contacts 93, 149, 150, 151, 186, 188, 189, 190, 191, 193, 195; decoy1 and decoy2 the same cluster. Complementary-face residues (loop D Trp55, loop E ~106-119, loop F ~163-168) are contacted essentially never. So all four chains dock into loop A (Tyr93) / loop B (Trp149) / loop C (Cys190-Cys191, Tyr193, Tyr195) - the aromatic box. decoy1 scores ipTM 0.8301, which README.md:465-467 quotes as the headline example of a false hit. Folding one ECD copy converts an occluded inter-subunit interface into free, aromatic, solvent-exposed surface, and the predictor docks native and composition-matched scrambles alike into it - which is precisely what the four models show. The construct therefore cannot host the declared orthosteric site either, not just the PAM site, and the CHRNA7 ipTMs (including the 0.830 decoy the README uses as its cautionary example) are scores against a pocket that does not exist in the biological assembly. `construct_basis` returning 'ectodomain' asserts a valid soluble-phase construct here, and for an obligate oligomer that assertion is false.

For CHRNA7 either fold five copies of the ECD or refuse the target, as is already done for GPCRs and transporters. Extend the README.md:479-508 disclosure to say that the orthosteric ECD site is also not hosted by a monomeric construct, so that the PfcACh-PAM-P1 decoy 0.830 is not read as a composition effect when it is at least partly a quaternary-structure artefact.
